Resources key) and were left alone, each with a reason in its row/not_imported_summary: EngineVersion, ProjectStats, ProjectResources, CompilerLocalization (package owns / regenerates each of these keys) and the two UI component instances (LoadingIcon, EngineInitializationUI), which are prefab components rather than assets.

OBJECT REFERENCES: 200 PPtr nodes were decoded in the configuration objects - 162 null in the shipped object (left null), 1 bound through a verified identity, 37 left null and listed in `needs_binding`. A shipped PPtr is (m_FileID, m_PathID) into resources.assets and those ids do not exist in this project, so binding them needs a path_id -> asset table (a later pass); nothing here was invented, and each needs_binding record carries the target class, name, path_id and (for information only, never auto-bound) whether this project holds same-named same-typed assets.

CONSEQUENCE OF THE UNBOUND REFERENCES: EngineConfiguration.CustomInitializationUI and AudioConfiguration.CustomAudioMixer are left null, which makes the engine fall back to the package's own resources - Engine.LoadInternalResource<ScriptableUIBehaviour>("EngineInitializationUI") (RuntimeInitializer.cs:47-49) and Engine.LoadInternalResource<AudioMixer>("DefaultMixer") (AudioManager.cs:91). The engine initialises with a working default in both cases, but audio routing (the shipped game used the 'WitchTrials' mixer with Master/Bgm/Sfx/Voice group paths) and the game's own initialization UI (WitchTrials.Views.EngineInitializationUiModified) are not reproduced. InputConfiguration.InputActions is null as well and its target lives in another serialized file (m_FileID 1), so no mapping inside resources.assets can ever recover it; combined with the shipped ProcessLegacyBindings = false this leaves input inert until the game's .inputactions asset is supplied. Actor metadata (Metadata.metas[*].CustomSpriteMaterial, 34 references in all) points at the materials 'MaskableTransparent' / 'MaskableTransparentToned_1', which do not exist anywhere in this project (the tool re-checks at run time and records the candidates it finds), so sprites fall back to Naninovel's default material.

[SerializeReference]: all 54 managed references in the decode (actor metadata `customData`) are Unity's null sentinel (raw_id -2), so they are written as null - which is exactly what the shipped object holds. The four objects that carry a trailing ManagedReferencesRegistry (BackgroundsConfiguration, CharactersConfiguration, ChoiceHandlersConfiguration, TextPrintersConfiguration) therefore need no registry restored; the registry node is reported per row and skipped, not applied.

DUPLICATE TYPE: `WitchTrials.Models.WitchTrialsChoiceHandlersConfiguration` occurs twice in the shipped build. The engine's lookup key is the type name, so the object whose Resources key matches it (path_id 1481, m_Name 'WitchTrialsChoiceHandlersConfiguration') owns WitchTrialsChoiceHandlersConfiguration.asset. The other one (path_id 1465, m_Name 'ChoiceHandlersConfigurationWitchTrials') carries the same single field DefaultCriticalChoiceHintEnabled = true and differs only in the m_Name bytes (both objects are 76 bytes), and it is restored under its own decoded name so nothing is lost; the engine will never load it by type name. If you would rather not carry an asset the engine cannot reach, delete ChoiceHandlersConfigurationWitchTrials.asset after the run - nothing else depends on it.

VERSION DRIFT, BOTH DIRECTIONS: the decoder took each layout from *this* project's C# sources and all 31 walks close exactly, so every decoded name should resolve. If one does not, the row lists it in fields_skipped with the reason and the C# default is kept - no value is dropped silently, and each imported row carries `values_accounted` (fields_applied + fields_skipped == values_total) so the accounting can be checked from the report. The other direction is invisible by construction: a field that exists in this package but was absent in the shipped build keeps its C# default and this pass cannot tell.
